title: Minimum Absolute Difference in Sliding Submatrix
summary: Given an m x n integer matrix, calculate the minimum absolute difference between any two distinct values in every k x k submatrix.
statement: Given an m x n integer matrix, calculate the minimum absolute difference between any two distinct values in every k x k submatrix. Return a (m - k + 1) x (n - k + 1) array where each element represents the minimum absolute difference in the corresponding k x k submatrix. If all elements in a submatrix are the same, the result is 0.
constraints: grid has at most 30 rows and columns; 1 <= k <= min(rows,columns).
For every contiguous k by k submatrix, compare distinct values only.
Return zero when a submatrix has fewer than two distinct values.
hints: In one window, the minimum difference among distinct values occurs between adjacent values in sorted order.
Collect a set for each k by k window, sort it, and scan neighboring gaps.
For each top-left coordinate, sort the window’s distinct values and append min(next-current), defaulting to zero.
Any nonadjacent sorted pair has a gap at least as large as one intervening adjacent gap, so checking neighbors is sufficient.
editorial: Any nonadjacent sorted pair has a gap at least as large as one intervening adjacent gap, so checking neighbors is sufficient.

tests.explanation: Sorted distinct values are -2, 1, 3, and 8; the closest gap is two.
Each one-cell submatrix has only one distinct value, producing zeros.
